issues.legal_issue: A later suit is barred by res judicata when the court that decided the former suit could have tried the later suit under its pecuniary jurisdiction at the time the former suit was filed, even if a later increase in the property's assessed value would place the later suit outside that court's jurisdiction.
material_facts: A former suit sought a declaration of title to land and cancellation of a sale deed; the claim was dismissed after the trial court found the asserted title unproved, and the dismissal became final.
A later suit sought possession of the same land on the same title allegations.

The former suit's jurisdictional value, based on the land revenue assessment at that time, was within the trial court's pecuniary limit; the later suit's higher value resulted from an increase in the assessment.
The parties admitted that the case otherwise fell within the rule of res judicata.
issues.conclusion: The former court's competence was to be assessed as of the filing of the former suit. Because it could then have tried the later suit, the later suit was barred by res judicata notwithstanding the subsequent increase in assessed value.
issues.legal_principle: For res judicata, the competence of the court that decided the former suit to try the later suit is determined by that court's jurisdiction when the former suit was brought. A subsequent increase in the value of the property does not undo that competence if the later suit would have been within the court's jurisdiction at the earlier time. The judgment relies on this as a well-settled rule and cites no specific statutory provision or earlier case for it.

predicates.later_possession_suit_follows_final_titl: A possession suit follows a final decision in an earlier suit seeking a determination of title to the property.
predicates.same_property_and_title_claim: The later suit concerns the same property and rests on the same asserted title claim as the earlier suit.
predicates.former_court_could_try_later_suit_at_for: At the time the earlier suit was filed, the court that decided it had jurisdiction to try the later suit based on the circumstances then existing.

issues.definition: If a possession suit follows a final title suit concerning the same property and title claim, and the former court could have tried the later suit when the former suit was filed, the later suit is barred by res judicata.
